name: Archean Chemical Industries Ltd
title: Archean Chemical Industries Ltd - 543657 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Archean Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 17.5% YoY to INR89.3 crore, but management withdrew SOP guidance and H1 EBITDA was flat.
summary.overview: Standalone total income rose 32% YoY to INR305.4 crore and EBITDA rose 17.5% YoY to INR89.3 crore, with PAT of INR43.2 crore. Consolidated EBITDA for H1 fell 5.2% YoY to INR147.3 crore on a weak Q1. Bromine volumes and revenue grew strongly YoY, while industrial salt volumes fell 9% YoY and Acume posted a one-quarter EBITDA loss of about INR1 crore. Management cut the FY27 SOP volume outlook to 3,500-4,000 tons from 9,000-10,000 tons, and the Odisha semiconductor project (SiCSem) started civil works.

segments.name: Industrial salt
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR161 crore, up 9% YoY, with volumes down 9% YoY to about 812,000 tons because of customer deferrals tied to PVC and caustic soda. Management says H1 volume was about 1.8-1.9 million tons and it has high confidence in 4.2-4.3 million tons for FY27. Realisation was lifted by mix, and the cost per ton stayed flat QoQ.

segments.name: Bromine
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR127 crore, up 76% YoY. Volume was about 4,100 tons, up 29% YoY, and H1 volume was 8,300 tons, up 18% YoY. Realisation was up 36% YoY and stable QoQ. Unscheduled power cuts cost about 6-7% of output in the quarter.

segments.name: Acume (bromine derivatives)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR36 crore, up 81% YoY, with finished derivative volume of 2,115 tons, up 56% YoY. The quarter posted an EBITDA loss of about INR1 crore from adverse mix, one-time period costs and an inventory revaluation. H1 revenue was INR66 crore, up 51% YoY, and H1 was EBITDA positive. Capacity utilisation was about 40%.

segments.name: SOP (sulphate of potash)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume was 444 tons and value INR2.18 crore; H1 volume was about 2,400 tons. FY27 volume is now guided at 3,500-4,000 tons, versus the earlier 9,000-10,000 tons, because trials were delayed about a quarter and KTMS feedstock output was below plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bromine volume is expected at the lower end of the 18,000-20,000 ton guidance, with recovery of the 6-7% power-cut loss in H2.
FY27 salt volume is expected at 4.2-4.3 million tons, with an attempt to exceed 4.5 million tons. Management says the 4.5 million ton target has uncertainty.
Bromine average yield is expected to hold at about INR300/kg for the full year and at minimum each quarter.
SOP FY27 volume is cut to 3,500-4,000 tons. FY28 SOP throughput is expected to be significantly above this year, with pricing of USD 600-700/ton.
Management does not give earnings guidance. The Hajipir road re-routing (completed early October) is expected to mitigate most of the 15-30% increase in transport cost from Q3.
Bromine debottlenecking Phase 1 (25,000 tons run rate next year) is expected to finish in FY27. Flame retardant and the next bromine expansion are targeted for FY27-FY28 to FY28-FY29.

The Odisha semiconductor (SiCSem) project is about USD 240 million total, with a little under half funded by ISM. Management expects INR1,000-1,100 crore more investment, largely through debt, and 24 months of construction end to end.
Core chemical capex is to stay within the depreciation curve, with debt-to-equity of 0.6-0.7 (about 0.7 over three years).
capex_capacity: SiCSem project in Odisha: civil works started in Q2, environmental clearance received in mid-October, and first equipment consignments shipping. Construction is about 18-24 months; INR462.8 crore invested to date.

Brine field expansion: Phase 1 (4,000 hectares of an 8,000-hectare expansion, total 24,000 hectares) is in CWIP and expected to go live within about a quarter. Brine field expansion drives both salt and bromine volumes.
SOP plant modification is expected to be capitalised by end-FY27. Total CWIP is about INR120 crore, of which about INR80 crore is chemicals and about INR40 crore is SiCSem.
Bromine debottlenecking is on schedule, with some minor delays. Management expects completion in FY27.
Fleet: 100 new company-owned trailers were added in Q2 and a Kandla yard was commissioned. Electric trucks are at pilot stage, limited by charging downtime on about 300-400 km routes.
demand_pricing: Caustic soda and chlorine prices remain volatile. PVC demand is weak, with lower operating rates and deferrals from large salt customers; management expects a PVC price rebound this quarter.

Bromine exports are strong and pricing there is stable. Domestic bromine pricing is under pressure from agro and pharma slowdown and higher competitive intensity, which management says has not hit its own yields.

Industrial salt: about 80% of volume is on 18-24 month long-term contracts and about 10-20% is spot. Spot share has risen above 10% because of rescheduling. New export orders came from Vietnam and Oman.

Input inflation: industrial HSD rose from about INR87/litre in Q2 FY26 to about INR136 in Q2 FY27. Coal and propanol rose about 40% YoY, and sulphur more than doubled. Management expects cost pressure to continue through the rest of this year.
Oil and gas (oilfield specialty products at Oren Hydrocarbons): order traction is weak, with only campaign orders and no structured offtake. Management expects a ramp-up from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will bromine volume fall short of 18,000-20,000 tons, and will salt reach 4.5 million tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Bromine is expected at the lower end of guidance, with H2 recovery from power-cut losses of 6-7%. Salt is pegged at 4.2-4.3 million tons with an attempt to pass 4.5 million, and PVC-linked deferrals are the main uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Hajipir road completion lift H2 EBITDA, and is there a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transport costs rose 15-30% from the diversions and that most of this should be mitigated from Q3. Risks are fuel prices (Q2 averaged about INR130 per litre, with further upside), winter recovery issues, and bromine volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex and debt will SiCSem need, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD 240 million total, of which a little under half is ISM-funded. Another INR1,000-1,100 crore is needed, largely debt, front-loaded. Interim construction milestones will be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SOP guidance cut and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 SOP volume was about 2,400 tons. FY27 is now 3,500-4,000 tons because of a one-quarter trial delay and feedstock (KTMS) shortfalls. FY28 pricing is expected at USD 600-700/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q2 salt realisation high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to grade and geography mix, with more deferrals in lower-priced geographies. It said this was not a deliberate pricing change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Acume operating rate and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished production of 2,115 tons was about 40% of capacity. Management expects utilisation to rise over the next couple of quarters, though organic compound mix is weak.

risks_watch: Fuel and sulphur cost inflation, with management flagging that a further fuel increase could erode much of the logistics saving.
PVC-linked customer deferrals in salt, which could keep volumes below the 4.5 million ton target.
Power-cut downtime at bromine, and winter recovery issues.
The Hajipir land lease extension with the Gujarat government is still pending; management says there is no operational impact yet.
SOP feedstock (KTMS) and trial execution; FY28 volume and pricing remain unconfirmed.
Funding and execution risk on the SiCSem project (INR1,000-1,100 crore of debt-led funding, instrument not finalised).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the bromine and road-logistics recovery, but cautious on salt volumes, fuel and sulphur costs, and SOP, where guidance was cut. Management declined to give earnings guidance and deferred several questions (Offgrid commercialisation, SOP FY28 volume, electric trucks) to later updates.

growth.why: Management gives no earnings guidance; volume guidance is mixed: bromine held at lower end of 18,000-20,000 t, salt 4.2-4.3 Mt, but SOP cut to 3,500-4,000 t from 9,000-10,000 t, and H1 consolidated EBITDA fell 5.2%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Input inflation is running hard: industrial HSD rose from about INR87/litre to about INR136 (+56%), coal and propanol up about 40% YoY and sulphur more than doubled, with management expecting cost pressure through the rest of this year; Hajipir road savings (15-30% transport cost increase largely mitigated from Q3) are the only offset, and consolidated H1 EBITDA fell 5.2% YoY.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brine field expansion Phase 1 (4,000 of 8,000 hectares, total 24,000 ha) is in CWIP and expected live within about a quarter, bromine debottlenecking to 25,000 t/yr run rate is due in FY27, and the SOP plant modification is capitalised by end-FY27; SiCSem (USD 240 million, INR462.8 crore invested) runs 18-24 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Salt guided at 4.2-4.3 million t with a push past 4.5 million t, but PVC-linked deferrals cut Q2 volume 9% YoY to about 812,000 t; bromine at lower end of 18,000-20,000 t with H2 recovery of 6-7% power-cut loss; SOP cut to 3,500-4,000 t from 9,000-10,000 t.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it will look at investing another INR1,000-1,100 crore largely through debt for SiCSem, and utilisation is only about 40% at Acume, so the new capex is firm in intent while the instrument is not yet finalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no earnings guidance and cut SOP volume by roughly 60% at the midpoint, with bromine only at the lower end and salt volume uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel rose to about INR130/litre in Q2 with more upside flagged, sulphur more than doubled, SOP FY27 already cut, and bromine power-cut losses of 6-7% of output could push volumes to the bottom of guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Flame retardant and the next bromine expansion are targeted for FY27-FY28 to FY28-FY29, but no firm dates are given and Offgrid commercialisation was deferred.

rows.label: SOP FY28 volume and pricing step-up
rows.why: Management expects FY28 SOP throughput well above FY27's 3,500-4,000 t at USD 600-700/ton, but trials and KTMS feedstock are unconfirmed and the FY28 volume question was deferred.

rows.label: Oil and gas ramp-up at Oren Hydrocarbons
rows.why: Order traction is weak with only campaign orders and no structured offtake, and management expects a ramp-up only from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: New salt export orders from Vietnam and Oman
rows.why: New export orders came in from Vietnam and Oman, and export share of revenue rose to 79% in Q2 from 75% a year earlier, though salt spot share above 10% limits pricing visibility.

tone.note: Management was confident on bromine exports, the Hajipir road logistics recovery and the brine expansion, but cautious on salt volumes, fuel and sulphur costs and SOP, where guidance was cut; analysts pressed on SOP, salt volume, SiCSem funding and capex, and management deferred several questions.
